name: Ambassadors
overview: Scripture portrays ambassadors as messengers sent by leaders to communicate with other nations, often bearing important declarations or requests. For example, Moses sent envoys to the king of Edom explaining Israel's journey (Numbers 20:14), and Israel sent messengers to the Amorite king Sihon (Numbers 21:21). Ambassadors also appear in strategic or diplomatic contexts, such as Benhadad's bold demands to King Ahab of Israel (1 Kings 20:2-3) and Jephthah's message to the Ammonite king (Judges 11:12). These passages emphasize the role of ambassadors as representatives who carry the authority and intentions of their sovereigns in matters of peace, negotiation, or conflict.
